title: Cold stellarator coils that outlast power plant lifetime
abstract: We show that a two order-of-magnitude reduction in stellarator coil peak neutron flux and heating can be achieved by moving coils much farther from the plasma if the plasma shape may change slightly and the vessel shielding is increased. Alternating coil and plasma optimizations move the closest coils of our main design over 25 cm out, without substantial degradation in key engineering and physics requirements. The field error decreases and the plasma boundary moves about 1 cm on average. Such coils would be at 4.2 K, use only one third to half the superconducting tape of the original, and require no replacement during the plant's lifetime. This reduced coil flux and heating could significantly enhance the viability of stellarator power plants.
